stories.headline: Modi declares victory over Maoists in Bastar: what it really means
stories.question: Has India really beaten the Maoist insurgency, and what comes next for Bastar?
stories.dek: The government says yes, because the Maoist leadership is gone and affected districts have shrunk. But Modi says "this is not the end", and critics want troops cut and Adivasi rights restored.

so_far.text: Naxalism is India's armed Maoist insurgency, which aims to overthrow the state by force. Bastar, in Chhattisgarh, saw heavy fighting. In 2025, Bastar police reported 256 Maoists, 23 security personnel and 46 civilians killed. In October 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Maoist-affected districts had fallen from 125 to three over 11 years. On 30 March 2026, Home Minister Amit Shah told the Lok Sabha that India was Naxal-free. On 19 May 2026, at Jagdalpur, he declared Bastar Naxal-free. In late July 2026, police arrested Misir Besra, described as the last absconding top Maoist leader.

what_happened.text: On 8 November 2026, Modi spent Diwali with security personnel in Bastar. There he said India had won its long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. He called ending Naxalism a milestone. He said the achievements inspire, but added: "this is not the end of the journey -- I repeat, this is not the end." He linked it to other goals, such as Article 370 and Viksit Bharat, the plan for a developed India. Reports of the speech gave no figures on deaths, surrenders or districts still affected.

steps.text: An armed insurgency needs leaders to plan, fighters to act, and areas where it can hide and recruit.
Shah said the Maoists' top decision-making bodies once had 21 members, and only two remained by March 2026.
Besra's arrest in July 2026 removed the last absconding top leader; ThePrint says both top bodies are now defunct.
With leaders gone and affected districts down to a handful, the government says the armed movement is finished.
But 'Naxal-free' is a declaration, not a published count; the Bastar speech coverage gave no new figures.

analogy.text: Think of an army whose generals have all been captured. Soldiers may still hold guns, but no one draws up plans, moves supplies or picks targets. The government's case is that the Maoists are now in that state: leaderless, so unable to run an organised campaign.
analogy.breaks: An insurgency is not only an army. Small groups can act without generals, and local complaints over land and rights do not end with arrests.

for_you.text: For most readers outside Bastar, the direct effect is small. For people in Bastar, the questions are whether the heavy security presence shrinks and what happens to Adivasi rights. For everyone, watch how the 'dimagi Naxal' idea is used. Modi said such people should be identified and isolated. Congress's Jairam Ramesh called that desperation; Kiren Rijiju said it does not target the opposition.

lesson.concept: How a government judges an insurgency is over
lesson.big_idea: An insurgency needs leaders, fighters and territory. Governments declare victory when all three shrink sharply, but 'over' is a judgment call, not one single number.

steps.title: Three things an insurgency needs
steps.text: Leaders decide strategy and targets. Fighters, called cadres, carry out attacks. Territory gives them places to hide, train and recruit. Weaken one, and the other two suffer.

steps.title: Measure one: territory
steps.text: Governments count 'affected districts', places with regular insurgent violence. Modi said Maoist-affected districts fell from 125 to three over 11 years.

steps.title: Measure two: leadership
steps.text: Shah said the Maoists' top bodies once had 21 members and only two by March 2026. In July 2026, Misir Besra, the last absconding top leader, was arrested.

steps.title: Measure three: violence
steps.text: Deaths and attacks show whether fighters are still active. In 2025, Bastar police reported 256 Maoists, 23 security personnel and 46 civilians killed.

steps.title: Declaring 'over' is a judgment
steps.text: No single number marks the end. Leaders weigh all three measures and declare victory. Coverage of the 8 November speech gave no fresh figures on any of them.

example.setup: Imagine a made-up state with 20 districts. Assume rebels were active in 10 of them, had 10 top leaders, and carried out 100 attacks a year.

lines.label: Territory now
lines.note: Fewer places to hide and recruit.

lines.label: Leaders now
lines.calc: Assume 10 leaders fall to 0 at large
lines.note: No one left to plan or direct.

lines.label: Attacks now
lines.note: Fighters weakened, but not gone.

lines.label: Share of attacks left
lines.note: Small, but some violence remains.

lines.label: Government's call
lines.note: A judgment based on all three measures together.

example.result: All three measures fell sharply, so the government declares victory. But one district and five attacks remain. That is why 'free' can mean 'mostly over', and why a leader may add 'this is not the end'.

practice.q: Same made-up state, but leaders at large fall only from 10 to 5, and attacks fall from 100 to 60. Is a victory claim strong?
practice.answer: Leaders: 5 of 10 still at large, so half the leadership remains. Attacks: 60 ÷ 100 = 60% remain. Two of the three measures are still high, so a victory claim would be weak.

stories.headline: UN climate summit opens in Turkey with low hopes
stories.question: Can the UN climate summit in Turkey achieve anything while droughts, floods and heat raise the pressure?
stories.dek: COP31 opens in Antalya on 9 November with modest goals. It cannot order any country to act. It can push countries to file their climate plans, and it can push money towards poorer nations.

so_far.text: Every year, countries in the UN climate treaty meet at a summit called a COP. At COP29 in Baku, they set a goal of $300 billion a year in climate finance for developing countries by 2035, up from $100 billion. COP30 in Brazil ended without a roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels in its main text. Brazil's presidency promised a separate, non-binding roadmap by COP31. It also urged every country to submit its overdue national climate plan.

what_happened.text: COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 in Antalya, Turkey. Turkey hosts, and its environment minister, Murat Kurum, is COP31 president. Australia's Chris Bowen runs the formal negotiations. In September, Kurum said Turkey has the final say, a possible source of friction. Expectations are low. The New York Times headlined its opening report 'With Hopes Low and Temperatures High'. The Christian Science Monitor said the summit opens 'with modest goals'. DW reports that droughts, floods and extreme heat are pushing delegates to move from pledges to action. Departing UN Secretary-General António Guterres told AP it is 'a moment of truth'.

steps.text: No world government can force countries to cut emissions, so each country writes its own climate plan.
COP decisions need every country's agreement, so the final text often shrinks to what the most reluctant country accepts.
India says greater ambition must be backed by climate finance and technology, so money becomes a central bargaining point.
COP30 also left work unfinished: no fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap in its main text, only a promised separate, non-binding one.
So COP31 will be judged on small steps: overdue national plans, the promised fossil-fuel roadmap, and money.

lesson.concept: How climate summits work without a world boss
lesson.big_idea: No one can order a country to cut pollution. A COP adds up each country's own plan and finds the gap. It then uses pressure and money to make the gap smaller.

steps.title: No one gives orders
steps.text: There is no world government for climate. Under the Paris Agreement, each country writes its own plan, called an NDC (nationally determined contribution). The plan says how much the country will cut its emissions. No one can force a bigger number.

steps.title: Everyone must agree
steps.text: Decisions at a COP, the yearly UN climate summit, need consensus: no country formally objects. So one reluctant country can hold back the text. Final deals often reflect only what every country can accept.

steps.title: Add up plans, find the gap
steps.text: Experts add up all the national plans and compare the total with the cut needed to limit warming. The difference is called the 'ambition gap'. Summits use peer pressure to get countries to raise their plans.

steps.title: Money moves the numbers
steps.text: Poorer countries often need help to cut more. That help is climate finance. COP29 set a goal of $300 billion a year for developing countries by 2035. India says greater ambition must be backed by finance and technology.

example.setup: Imagine a tiny world of four countries. Together they must cut 100 tonnes of pollution to stay safe. Each writes its own plan. The summit can only add them up.

lines.label: Plans on the table
lines.note: Each country chose its own number.

lines.label: Total pledged
lines.note: This is all the summit has to work with.

lines.label: The gap
lines.note: Short of what is needed, and no one can order more.

lines.label: Finance offer
lines.calc: Assume D cuts 10 tonnes if paid
lines.note: Money changes a poorer country's plan.

lines.label: New gap
lines.note: Smaller, but still open for the next summit.

example.result: The summit forced no one. It halved the gap, from 20 tonnes to 10, by adding up plans, applying pressure and bringing money. That is how a COP achieves things: in steps, not leaps.

apply.text: COP31 in Antalya works the same way. It cannot order cuts. It can press countries to file the overdue plans Brazil asked for. It can also deliver the promised non-binding fossil-fuel roadmap and turn the $300 billion goal into real money. This is the logic behind India's position: Bhupender Yadav says greater ambition must be backed by finance and technology.

practice.q: Same tiny world, but the safe cut is 120 tonnes. Plans: A 50, B 30, C 20, D 0. D offers 15 tonnes if paid. What is the gap before and after?
practice.answer: Total pledged: 50 + 30 + 20 + 0 = 100 tonnes. Gap before: 120 − 100 = 20 tonnes. With D's paid-for 15 tonnes, the total is 115. Gap after: 120 − 115 = 5 tonnes. Money closed three-quarters of the gap.

stories.headline: Nvidia orders independent probe after report that China targeted its CEO
stories.question: Why is Nvidia investigating its own CEO over a foreign intelligence operation?
stories.dek: Reports say China's spy agency recruited a woman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The boss cannot judge his own case, so independent directors and outside lawyers will run Nvidia's probe.

so_far.text: Nvidia sells advanced AI chips. The US bars most of its top-tier chips from sale to customers in China, over national security concerns. One buyer of Nvidia's advanced chips was Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. Nvidia says claims that Megaspeed diverted chips were investigated and debunked last year. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and CEO, earlier told Bloomberg his dealings with Megaspeed were 'completely normal and not unusual'. Senator Elizabeth Warren had urged Huang and Nvidia's board to answer Congress about press reports on Megaspeed.

lesson.concept: How a company investigates its own boss
lesson.big_idea: When a company's own boss is under question, he cannot run the inquiry. Directors with no ties to him take charge, and they hire outside lawyers to find the facts.

steps.title: The board watches the boss
steps.text: Shareholders own a listed company. They elect a board of directors to guard their interests. The CEO runs the company day to day, but answers to the board.

steps.title: Insiders and independents
steps.text: Some directors are insiders, like the CEO. Others are independent directors: people with no job at the company and no business ties to its managers.

steps.title: Nobody judges their own case
steps.text: When the question is about the CEO, he has a conflict of interest, meaning a personal stake in the answer. So a committee of independent directors takes charge, as at Nvidia.

steps.title: Outside lawyers do the digging
steps.text: The committee hires outside counsel, a law firm independent of the managers. The lawyers interview staff, read records and report what they find to the committee.

steps.title: The board decides what follows
steps.text: The committee reports to the full board. The board then decides what to do: no action, new rules, or bigger changes. The CEO under review cannot steer that decision.

stories.question: Why are the US and European central banks preparing to raise interest rates again in December?
stories.dek: Prices are still rising too fast, and new US jobs data shows demand is strong. So the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank are both signalling a possible December rate rise.

so_far.text: In 2026, a jump in energy prices linked to the Iran war pushed inflation up. The European Central Bank (ECB) has raised rates twice this year to stop that jump becoming entrenched. On 29 October it held rates but signalled a possible December hike. Euro-area inflation is about twice its 2% target. In the US, prices rose 3.7% in a year, faster than pay. lesson.concept: How a rate rise cools inflation
lesson.big_idea: Central banks raise interest rates to make borrowing costlier. People and firms then borrow and spend less, demand cools, and prices rise more slowly.

steps.title: Inflation has a target
steps.text: Central banks aim for slow, steady price rises. The ECB's target is 2% a year. Euro-area inflation is now about twice that, which is why the ECB is worried.

steps.title: The policy rate prices money
steps.text: The central bank sets a policy rate. Banks build it into what they charge on loans. A quarter-point hike adds 0.25 percentage points to that rate.

steps.title: Costlier loans mean less spending
steps.text: When loans cost more, fewer people buy homes or cars on credit. Firms delay new shops and hire more slowly. Total demand cools, and price rises slow down.

steps.title: Hot jobs data means hot demand
steps.text: If employers keep hiring fast, people have income to spend. The central bank fears prices will not cool on their own. October's 165,000 new US jobs sent that signal.

steps.title: The real fear: a spiral
steps.text: A one-off energy jump can become entrenched if workers demand matching pay and firms raise prices again. The ECB says wages have not responded much yet, and wants to keep it that way.

apply.text: This is why both banks are eyeing December. The ECB has raised rates twice in 2026 to stop the energy jump becoming entrenched, and inflation is still about twice target. In the US, 165,000 new jobs suggest demand is hot, so markets see about an 80% chance of the same quarter-point step as in our example.

stories.question: Why has the rupee slid this year, and can new rules and rate hikes help?
stories.dek: Costly oil and foreign investors pulling money out have pushed the rupee down nearly 5% this year. New caps on speculative bets remove one source of pressure. They do not touch oil prices or investor flows.

so_far.text: The rupee hit a record low near 96.97 per dollar in May 2026. By 8 October it was close to that low again. Forex reserves, the RBI's stock of foreign currency, had dropped to about $734 billion from a $785 billion peak. On 10 October the RBI cut the limit for rupee bets without real dollar exposure to $5 million. It also opened a special dollar window for Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL. In October the RBI raised the repo rate, the rate at which it lends to banks, by 0.25 percentage points to 5.5%.

what_happened.text: Sebi, India's markets regulator, has brought exchange trading in line with the RBI's $5 million cap, down from $100 million. Domestic investors and foreign portfolio investors can now hold at most $5 million of rupee bets across all exchanges combined without proving real exposure. Cancelled contracts cannot be rebooked. Clients must confirm they are not hedging the same exposure at several banks. The rupee closed at 93.91 per dollar on 6 November, its strongest since 22 April, after its best week of 2026. On 5 November Uday Kotak said the RBI could raise the repo rate by another 50–75 basis points.

steps.text: The rupee's price moves with demand for dollars. When more people need dollars, each dollar costs more rupees.
Costlier crude means importers need more dollars. Foreign investors selling Indian shares also swap rupees for dollars.
Speculators betting on a fall add extra one-sided dollar demand. The $5 million cap shrinks how much they can add.
A higher repo rate cools inflation and makes rupee assets pay more, which can draw foreign money back.
But neither tool lowers oil prices. The rupee's best week came when oil slid and foreigners bought nearly $3 billion of shares.

lesson.concept: How capping speculative bets can steady the rupee
lesson.big_idea: The rupee's price depends on how many people want dollars. Speculators betting on a fall add extra dollar demand. Capping their bets removes some pressure, but not the real needs behind it.

steps.title: Price comes from dollar demand
steps.text: The rupee's value is how many rupees one dollar costs. When more people want dollars than sell them, each dollar costs more rupees. That is what 'the rupee falls' means.

steps.title: Real users need dollars
steps.text: Oil importers pay in dollars, so costlier crude raises their need. Foreign investors leaving India swap rupees for dollars too. Mint lists both as drivers of the rupee's fall this year.

steps.title: Speculators can add pressure
steps.text: A currency derivative is a contract to buy dollars later at a price fixed now. Someone with no import bill who buys one is simply betting the rupee will fall. That adds one-sided demand.

steps.title: The cap shrinks the bet
steps.text: Bets without underlying exposure, meaning no real dollar need, are now capped at $5 million across all exchanges combined. The old limit was $100 million. Genuine hedgers can still go higher with documents.

steps.title: Rates work on the real side
steps.text: A higher repo rate, now 5.5%, cools inflation and makes rupee savings pay more. That can attract foreign money. It works slowly and cannot lower oil prices.

Sebi and the RBI capped bets without real exposure at $5 million, down from $100 million.

sections.title: World
sections.gist: US moves to block Iran's land trade, Europeans join Ukraine talks, the ANC suffers its worst-ever result, and France sees a fourth protest weekend.

items.headline: US sets up 20-member task force to block Iran's land routes
items.text: On 8 November Al Jazeera reported that the US has set up Task Force Iron Gate, based in Tampa, Florida. Its job is to stop Iran moving weapons, sanctioned goods and illicit money across its land borders and the Caspian Sea. It also covers dual-use technology, meaning items with both civilian and military uses. The team has 20 civilian and military members and will work with other US government agencies. Separately, on 8 November falling shrapnel from a Houthi attack hit an Aramco tower in Riyadh. Saudi authorities said no one was hurt. Iran also executed three men over 'armed unrest' linked to the January protests. It is not yet known when the task force will start operating.
items.background: The US already runs a naval blockade of Iran. The new task force is meant to close the land and Caspian Sea routes that a blockade at sea cannot reach.
items.why: It extends US pressure on Iran from the sea to its land borders and the Caspian Sea.

items.headline: Europeans to join Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, says France
items.text: On 8 November France's foreign minister said European representatives will take part in the talks on Ukraine being held in Abu Dhabi. Until now, the negotiations have been associated with US President Donald Trump. On the same day, AP reported that the Kremlin, Russia's government, hopes the US election shake-up will not change Trump's approach to the Ukraine negotiations. Neither report says when the next round in Abu Dhabi will happen. It is not yet known what role the Europeans will play at the table, or whether Russia will accept their presence.
items.background: Russia and Ukraine are at war. Talks to end it are taking place in Abu Dhabi, and Trump has been leading the US negotiating effort.
items.why: Who sits at the table shapes any deal; Europe is joining, and Russia is watching US politics closely.

items.headline: ANC slumps to worst-ever result in South Africa's local elections
items.text: On 8 November DW reported that the ANC recorded its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal elections. Municipal elections choose local councils. Voters blamed the ANC for shortages of water and electricity. South Africa faces a second problem. On 2 November the Trump administration told the US Congress it will remove South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA from 1 January 2027. AGOA is a US scheme that gives some African countries duty-free access to the US market, meaning their goods enter without import taxes. Watch for final seat counts and for how councils are formed.
items.background: The ANC (African National Congress) is a major South African party. In these local elections, voters punished it over water and power shortages.
items.why: Failing basic services cost the ANC votes, and South Africa loses duty-free US trade access from 1 January 2027.

items.headline: Two trains collide near Giza in Egypt, killing seven
items.text: On 8 November the BBC reported that two trains travelling in the same direction collided outside the city of Giza in Egypt. Several carriages came off the track. Seven people died and more than 100 were injured. India Today put the number of injured at 112 and said both were passenger trains. The sources do not say what caused the crash. It is not yet known whether Egyptian authorities have opened an investigation or when any findings will be published.
items.background: The crash happened outside Giza, Egypt. The two trains were moving in the same direction, so one ran into the other from behind.
items.why: Seven deaths and over 100 injuries make this a serious passenger rail accident; its cause is not yet known.

items.headline: Clashes in Paris on fourth weekend of French protests
items.text: On Saturday 7 November clashes broke out in Paris as new protests took place across France, Dawn reported. It was the fourth weekend in a row of demonstrations. The New York Times described the protests as part of an 'autumn of discontent'. These reports do not set out the protesters' demands or give crowd numbers. It is not yet known whether protests will continue on Saturday 14 November, which would make a fifth weekend.
items.background: France has seen demonstrations every Saturday for four weeks. The New York Times calls this period an 'autumn of discontent'.
items.why: Four weekends of protests, now with clashes in Paris, point to sustained unrest in a major European country.

sections.title: India
sections.gist: The TDP-led NDA sweeps Andhra's rural polls despite Jagan's rigging claims; police hold two gangsters abroad, in the US and Ethiopia.

items.headline: TDP-led NDA sweeps Andhra Pradesh rural local body polls
items.text: Results reported on 8 November show the TDP-led NDA winning Andhra Pradesh's rural local body elections. The NDA won 499 of 582 ZPTC seats (district council seats), about six in every seven. It won 5,861 of 7,768 MPTC seats (mandal, or block-level, council seats), about three in every four. The TDP alone took 406 ZPTCs and 4,806 MPTCs. On 5 November YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the coalition of manipulating every stage, from nominations to counting. He alleged blocked nominations, attacks on YSRCP agents and inflated votes. It is not yet known whether the YSRCP will take its complaints to the courts or election authorities.
items.background: The TDP, with BJP and allies, governs Andhra Pradesh; Jagan Mohan Reddy's YSRCP is the main opposition.
items.why: Rural councils control local spending on roads, water and schemes; the result shows the ruling alliance's grip on villages.

items.headline: Bishnoi gang's 'Hari Boxer' held in US; Punjab gangster deported
items.text: On 8 November Rajasthan Police said Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat, alias Hari Boxer, was detained in the US by ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement). Efforts are underway to bring him to India. Police say he supplied weapons to the Bishnoi-Godara gang and link him to the firing outside director Rohit Shetty's Mumbai home. More than 22 cases are registered against him in Rajasthan, including attempted murder and extortion. Separately, Punjab Police brought gangster Gurwinder, alias Afridi, back from Ethiopia on 8 November after a 10-month manhunt. He carried a ₹5 lakh reward. When Hari Boxer might be sent to India is not yet known.
items.background: Indian gangs such as the Lawrence Bishnoi network have members operating from abroad, so police depend on other countries to send them back.
items.why: Shows Indian police chasing gang members overseas, which depends on cooperation from countries like the US and Ethiopia.

sections.title: Your money & life
sections.gist: Delhi woke to thick Diwali smog with several areas above 400. Separately, CBSE's 2027 board exams begin on 16 February.

items.headline: Delhi wakes to thick smog on Diwali as AQI nears 'severe'
items.text: Delhi woke to thick smog on Diwali, 8 November. The city's AQI was close to the 'severe' mark, and several areas recorded readings above 400. AQI, the Air Quality Index, turns pollution levels into one number; higher means dirtier air. On Diwali eve, 7 November, Delhi's AQI was about 369, and several areas were already in the severe category. So the air got worse overnight, with more of the city crossing 400. It is not yet known how Diwali-night firecrackers will affect readings on 9 November.
items.background: On India's AQI scale, readings above 400 fall in the 'severe' category, the worst band.
items.why: Millions in Delhi are breathing air at or near the worst level on India's pollution scale.

items.headline: CBSE 2027 Class 10 and 12 board exams start 16 February
items.text: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the datesheet for its 2027 Class 10 and Class 12 board exams. Reports of the release appeared on 8 November. The exams begin on 16 February 2027. A datesheet is the official timetable. It shows which subject is tested on which day. CBSE has published a subject-wise schedule with it. The facts available here do not give the last exam date or the dates of individual papers. Students and parents should check the official schedule for their own subjects before planning revision.
items.background: CBSE runs the national board exams that millions of Class 10 and Class 12 students take each year.
items.why: Families now have a fixed start date, 16 February 2027, to plan revision, coaching and travel around.

sections.title: Markets & money
sections.gist: Sensex and Nifty closed almost flat in the Diwali Muhurat session. Oil slipped, and Berkshire bought back $9.6 billion of its shares.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty end Diwali Muhurat session slightly lower
items.text: Indian shares closed almost flat in the Diwali Muhurat session on 8 November. This session opened Samvat 2083. The Sensex ended at 80,999.40, down 28.62 points, or 0.04%. The Nifty ended at 24,986.40, down 43.95 points, or 0.18%. Early in the session the Sensex had jumped 401.80 points and the Nifty 79.15 points. Those gains faded by the close. The Sensex's early rise was about 14 times the size of its final fall. Reuters described the day as consolidation, meaning prices held steady, after a seven-day rally.
items.background: Muhurat trading is a short, symbolic stock market session on Diwali that marks the start of the new Hindu accounting year, called Samvat.
items.why: Many Indian families buy shares on Diwali for luck. A flat session means a calm start after a seven-day run.

items.headline: Oil futures slip on hopes for Middle East diplomacy
items.text: On 8 November oil futures fell as traders hoped for diplomacy in the Middle East, the Wall Street Journal reported. Oil futures are contracts to buy oil at a set price on a future date, so they show where traders expect prices to go. Separately, broker Upstox published its preview of the week after Muhurat trading, the special Diwali session. It named India and US inflation data, crude oil prices and FII activity among the key triggers to watch. FIIs are foreign institutional investors, such as overseas funds buying or selling Indian shares.
items.background: Middle East tensions affect oil prices, and traders' hopes for diplomacy pushed oil futures down on 8 November.
items.why: Upstox lists crude oil prices and foreign fund flows among the triggers for Indian markets after Diwali.

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway buys back $9.6 billion of shares as profit falls
items.text: Berkshire Hathaway bought back $9.6 billion of its own shares in the July–September quarter, AP reported on 7 November. In a buyback, a company buys its own shares, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice. Operating earnings, the profit from its businesses, fell nearly 6% to $12.7 billion, from $13.485 billion a year earlier. Insurance underwriting profit fell to $1.35 billion from $2.37 billion, a drop of about 43%. Net income, which also counts changes in the value of investments, was $22.1 billion, down more than 28%. Its cash pile rose to $377.4 billion from $365.5 billion at the end of June. The buyback equals about 2.5% of that cash.
items.background: Berkshire Hathaway is a giant US company that owns insurers and many other businesses and holds large stock investments.
items.why: There is no direct effect on Indian savers. It shows how a company holding $377.4 billion in cash chose to spend some.

sections.title: Tech & AI
sections.gist: A Claude Code setting leaked 2,539 secrets to public GitHub projects. Geoffrey Hinton warned of an AI attack on power grids.

items.headline: Claude Code setting leaked 2,539 secrets to public GitHub projects
items.text: Security firm Apiiro found 2,539 distinct secrets, such as passwords and access keys, in 1,994 public GitHub projects. The findings were reported on 7 November. Sixty-three organisations were affected. The secrets were saved when developers picked the 'Yes, and don't ask again' option in Claude Code, an AI coding tool. That choice stored credentials in a project settings file. When the file was uploaded publicly, anyone could read it. Apiiro checked 104,185 public copies of this file. Of these, 1,122, about 1 in 93, held real secrets, including 379 database passwords and 43 SSH logins. Recommended fix: change exposed credentials first, then remove the file from tracking and add it to .gitignore.
items.background: Developers store code on GitHub. Anything in a public project there, including settings files, can be read by anyone on the internet.
items.why: Indian developers and startups using AI coding tools could have exposed database passwords and server logins without knowing it.

items.headline: Geoffrey Hinton warns of an AI 'Chernobyl' attack on power grids
items.text: AI researcher Geoffrey Hinton told The Guardian that a major AI disaster may come soon. Futurism reported his remarks on 7 November. "Either later this year or next year we'll see Chernobyl, and that may be enough to make people really pay attention," he said. Chernobyl refers to the nuclear disaster. Hinton described an AI-powered attack on an energy-generating system that "causes a massive brownout". A brownout is a sharp drop in power supply. He said such an attack could knock out power grids for a long time. Futurism added that such an outage could also cripple banking. This is Hinton's prediction, not an event that has happened.
items.background: Futurism calls Hinton an 'AI godfather'. He has repeatedly warned about risks from the technology he helped build.
items.why: Power grids and banking run on networked computers everywhere, including India, so attacks on them would hit daily life directly.

sections.title: Science, health & climate
sections.gist: Pakistan's astronaut is set to be Tiangong's first foreign visitor, NASA unveils a Moon rover, and a heart drug fails.

items.headline: Pakistani astronaut set to be first foreigner on China's space station
items.text: On 7 November, China's space agency said a Pakistani payload specialist will fly to Tiangong, China's space station. A payload specialist is a crew member who goes up mainly to run experiments. No foreigner has visited Tiangong before, so this would be a first. The agency did not name the astronaut or give a date. It said only that the mission is expected by the end of the year. In April, China said two Pakistanis, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, had been chosen to start training in China. In October, Pakistan's planning minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission would fly on 25 November. Watch for China to confirm the date and which of the two will fly.
items.background: China built and runs Tiangong on its own. Until now, only Chinese astronauts have gone there on its Shenzhou crew flights.
items.why: Pakistan will be the first country to send someone to China's space station, a new step in their space partnership.

items.headline: NASA's new PROMISE rover will look for resources at Moon's south pole
items.text: NASA has unveiled PROMISE, a new rover for the Moon, Scientific American reported on 7 November. The name stands for Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping and In-Situ Exploration. 'In-situ' means studying things where they lie, not bringing them back to Earth. NASA based the design on its Mars rovers. PROMISE is due to launch in late 2028. A lander built by Blue Origin, the space company, will carry it to the Moon. Its main mission will last 18 months. During that time it will search for useful resources near the lunar south pole. NASA has not said what the rover might find.
items.background: Space agencies want to know what the Moon's south pole holds, because materials found there could support future crewed bases.
items.why: Mapping the Moon's resources helps decide where future bases can go and what astronauts can use there instead of bringing it from Earth.

items.headline: Novartis drops heart drug that cut Lp(a) but not heart attacks
items.text: Novartis is abandoning pelacarsen, CNN reported on 7 November. The drug targets Lp(a), a fatty particle in the blood whose level is set mostly by your genes. A trial enrolled 8,350 patients who had high Lp(a) and a past heart attack or stroke. The drug did lower Lp(a), by about 77% on average. But over nearly five years, about 12% of people in each group still had a serious heart or blood-vessel event. The drug group did no better than the comparison group. So lowering the blood number did not mean fewer heart attacks, strokes or heart deaths. The trial missed its main goal, and doctors were stunned.
items.background: High Lp(a) is an inherited heart risk. Doctors hoped that lowering it with a drug would prevent heart attacks and strokes.
items.why: It is a sharp reminder that improving a blood test result does not always mean a patient is protected from disease.

sections.title: Formula 1
sections.gist: Norris wins a wet Brazil race, Mercedes clinch their ninth team title, and Haas drops Ocon for the season.

items.headline: Norris wins wet Brazil race; Mercedes clinch constructors' title
items.text: Lando Norris of McLaren won the rain-hit São Paulo Grand Prix on 8 November. He started first and finished about 14.6 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen. Verstappen had started 21st, near the very back, so second place was a huge recovery. Isack Hadjar was third. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli led early but went off the track and finished fifth. His teammate George Russell also made errors and finished fourth. Even so, Mercedes won the 2026 constructors' championship, the title for the best team. It is their ninth such title, with three races still to go. On 7 November, F1 extended the Brazilian Grand Prix by five years, through 2035.
items.background: F1 has two titles each year: one for drivers, and the constructors' title for teams, which adds up both team drivers' points.
items.why: Mercedes have locked up the team title early, so the last three races decide only the drivers' title.

items.headline: Haas drops Ocon for the season; Racing Bulls near 2027 choice
items.text: Haas has told Esteban Ocon he will not race for the team again this season, The Race reported on 3 November. Rafael Camara took his seat in Brazil. It was Camara's first F1 race, at his home Grand Prix, and he finished 20th. Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said Ocon's axing 'surprised everybody at Haas'. Separately, Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said on 7 November that the team is 'almost there' on its 2027 driver line-up. He said the decision is not final yet. He expects to announce it in the coming weeks and said 'everyone will be happy'.
items.background: Teams pick their drivers for next season in the final months of the current one, so seats change hands quickly.
items.why: Haas changing drivers with races left is rare, and shows how quickly an F1 seat can be lost.

sections.title: Cricket — the masala
sections.gist: Pakistan beat India in the U-19 Asia Cup, while India A lead New Zealand A by 428 runs.

items.headline: Number-seven Hamza Zahoor's century wins it for Pakistan U-19
items.text: Pakistan beat India by three wickets in the Under-19 Asia Cup, The Hindu reported on 8 November. India were bowled out for 208, a modest total. Pakistan's top batters then fell early, and the chase wobbled. Hamza Zahoor came in at number seven. That spot usually goes to a lower-order batter, not a main run-scorer. He made an unbeaten 100 off 108 balls and took Pakistan home. Winning by three wickets means Pakistan reached the target with seven of their ten wickets gone. With only three wickets in hand, one more collapse could have swung the match to India.
items.background: The Under-19 Asia Cup is a youth tournament where future senior players first face their rivals, including India against Pakistan.
items.why: India lost to Pakistan in the age group where future senior stars are found and tested.

items.headline: India A build 428-run lead; Badoni replaces injured Patidar
items.text: India A declared at 464 for 5 against New Zealand A after 146 overs on day 2, The Hindu reported on 8 November. India A had resumed at 227 for 2. Captain Dhruv Jurel made 71, Tilak Varma 81 not out and Washington Sundar 50 not out. The lead is 428 runs, so New Zealand A must bat a long time just to make India A bat again. In other India A news, Rajat Patidar asked the BCCI, India's cricket board, to release him from the Rising Stars Asia Cup squad. He wants to manage existing injuries. Ayush Badoni takes his place.
items.background: India A is the country's second team. Its matches let selectors test players who are close to a senior India place.
items.why: Strong India A performances, like those by Jurel, Tilak and Washington, push players up the queue for senior India selection.
